shared_elements: carved stone surface with low-relief motifs
anthropomorphic form (A as a figure-shaped block; B as human figures)
incised linear detailing over the surface
circular/disc-like element (rosette-disc on A; round bosses/shield-like forms on B)
horizontal banded divisions of the surface
justification: Both are weathered stone monuments whose surfaces carry shallow relief and incised detail, including roughly circular disc-like elements and horizontally banded zones, and both are broadly anthropomorphic in subject. But A is a single free-standing, vertically massive block-figure with sparse, coarse, largely abstract emblems, whereas B is a flat horizontal frieze with a repeating procession of finely detailed profile figures beneath an inscribed band — the compositional logic and carving finesse have essentially nothing in common.
